items.prompt: Sliding window maintains what kind of region?
choices: A contiguous segment whose summary updates in amortized O(1) per move
items.whyRight: Left and right bound a contiguous slice.
whyWrong: Disconnected pairs are not a window.

items.prompt: Goal for a well-built window scan over n elements?
choices: O(n) total because each index enters/leaves at most once
items.whyRight: Right advances n times; left only moves forward.
whyWrong: Restarting from scratch each i is quadratic.
Log time cannot read all elements.

items.prompt: Variable window “longest substring with ≤ k distinct” tracks?
choices: Counts in the current window; shrink left when distinct exceeds k
A global sort of the string
items.whyRight: A frequency map plus two pointers enforces the constraint.
whyWrong: Sorting destroys index locality for substrings.
All prefixes is not a window.

items.prompt: Fixed window of size k sum updates by?
choices: Resumming k elements from scratch always
items.whyRight: One enter, one leave keeps the sum fresh.
whyWrong: Hashing is optional for other predicates.
Segment trees are heavier than needed.

items.prompt: When is sliding window the wrong first tool?
choices: The needed subset is not contiguous
You need a contiguous max average
items.whyRight: Non-contiguous subsets need other ideas (DP, hashing pairs, etc.).

items.prompt: A deque appears in window-maximum because it stores?
choices: Indices of candidates still inside the window in useful order
items.whyRight: Front is the max; back drops dominated values.
whyWrong: Prefix sums solve range sums differently.
